title: Chemical Cleaners and Heat Limits on DWV Piping
description: Many homeowners and property managers believe pouring boiling water or strong chemical drain cleaners down a clogged drain is a quick, safe fix. However, standard PVC drain-waste-vent (DWV) piping is typically rated for maximum continuous operating temperatures around 140°F (60°C). Pouring boiling water at 212°F (100°C) directly into PVC fittings can soften pipe walls and weaken glued joints over time. Furthermore, chemical cleaners generate exothermic reactions that produce intense local heat while corroding rubber seals and traps. Mechanics and professional plumbers recommend clearing blockages mechanically with a drain auger or hand snake to preserve pipe integrity and prevent costly hidden leaks.
